title: Razorfen Kraul
body: Razorfen Kraul is a warren of the quilboar burrowed deep into the Razorfen, the great thorn mass at the southern edge of the Barrens that they hold to be the body of their fallen boar god. Its tunnels wind through living bramble and down into a trench where great boars roam. The Razorfen tribe holds it under the crone Charlga Razorflank, and somewhere within they keep the captives they have dragged in from the plains.

parts.body: Among the captives a night elf, Heralath Fallowbrook, lies dying. He sent the dwarf Lonebrow to warn Falfindel, and his last plea is for his wife in Darnassus.

title: The Bat Roosts
body: Beyond the trench, at the far end of the warren, dim hollows open beneath the bramble where the Kraul bats roost. They hang in the dark in great numbers and drop on anything that stirs below, and the greater ones loose a shriek that chokes off any spell. They are a breed found nowhere else.

parts.body: The Royal Apothecary Society wants their guano for one of its most ambitious works, and Master Apothecary Faranell was delighted to have it.

title: Charlga Razorflank
body: Charlga Razorflank, the Crone, rules Razorfen Kraul. She is old and a caster of great power, and from her seat on a height near the heart of the warren she musters the army the Razorfen has been gathering. Her own tribe fills the halls around her, but the guards at the foot of her height are priests of the Death's Head.

parts.body: The southern Barrens were holy land to the tauren, who lived there for generations until the quilboar and others drove them off. Auld Stonespire of Thunder Bluff cannot forgive it, and wants her heart.

title: The Death's Head
body: Not every quilboar in the Kraul is of the Razorfen. Those who name themselves the Death's Head keep halls of their own under the prophet Aggem Thorncurse and their captain, Death Speaker Jargba, and their priests strike with shadow and their adepts with frost, where the tribe's shamans call on earth. They guard the crone's height, and keep a monstrous boar, Agathelos, penned behind a ward. For whom they speak, the Kraul does not tell.
